classification.difficultyReason: Check the supplied graphs against the two taught features: a straight line and passage through the origin.

content.prompt: Which of the graphs show a direct variation relationship?

spec.description: Four labelled qualitative Cartesian graphs in one comparison row. All axes and curves have arrowheads. No numerical scales, grid or origin label.
spec.mathematics: A is a rising straight line with positive y-intercept and negative x-intercept. B is a rising straight line through the origin. C is an increasing concave-down curve through the origin with a below-left continuation. D is a falling straight line with positive intercepts on both axes. Coordinates describe qualitative shapes only and are not numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All four choices remain visible in the question edition; the correct choice is supplied only in the answer.

answer.worked:
A direct variation graph is a straight line passing through the origin. Graph B has both properties.

Correct answer: B.
